questions.question: How much does the threshold-band for righteousness vary by tradition, office, emergency, and covenantal frame?
questions.why_live: rev0006 adds a threshold-band rule, but the archive still lacks a tradition- and role-sensitive map of how demanding righteousness becomes.

questions.question: Across major traditions, when should the portable core be typed as identity, incomplete identity, analogue, or rejection — and when is it only a public translation for shared institutions?
questions.why_live: rev0005 adds typed recognition statuses, but the archive has not yet mapped those statuses tradition by tradition.

questions.question: How far does righteous repair extend beyond direct culpable wrongdoing—to inherited advantage, structural damage, and institutions that still stand inside a damaged relation?
questions.why_live: rev0007 admits breach-responsive repair into canon, but the archive still has not settled how reparative standing travels when guilt, benefit, office, and historical continuity come apart.

questions.question: Is righteousness simply stronger than political legitimacy in public institutions, or does it track a partly different dimension of evaluation?
questions.why_live: rev0003 distinguishes legitimacy from righteousness, but the exact relation between them is not yet fully settled.

questions.question: When, if ever, may righteous office depart from ordinary publicity and contestability requirements under emergency or secrecy without collapsing into a theory of political exception?
questions.why_live: The office theory now imposes contestability and burdened-secrecy rules, but the archive still has not mapped which substitute safeguards are enough in classified, emergency, or highly asymmetric domains.

questions.question: Which defeaters of righteousness are remediable, and what minimally counts as requalification across persons, offices, and institutions?
questions.why_live: rev0009 adds avowal / interruption / repair / time as a working path of requalification, but the archive has not yet mapped which defeaters can be answered this way and which leave the original role-claim permanently defeated.

questions.question: How far can the archive sharpen its portable priority cues across traditions, offices, and emergencies without collapsing into a single ranking algorithm or erasing practical wisdom?
questions.why_live: rev0015 admits starter priority cues around need, vulnerability, reliance, creator-burden, and reversibility, but the archive still lacks tradition- and role-sensitive calibration for when those cues outrank one another.

questions.question: What temporal evidence and horizon are enough to move from an episode-level verdict to a warranted claim of righteous standing for persons, offices, or institutions?
questions.why_live: rev0012 distinguishes episode, standing, and trajectory, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive thresholds for how much repeat performance, repair, review, and time are enough to justify renewed reliance.

questions.question: How much inquiry, testimonial uptake, caution, and reversibility are enough for righteous action under uncertainty across different offices, emergency tempos, and kinds of risk?
questions.why_live: rev0013 adds an uncertainty discipline, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive thresholds for when inquiry is adequate, when precaution is required, and when revisable action is enough.

questions.question: Which burdens of righteous judgment, oversight, contestability, and repair are genuinely nondelegable across offices, institutions, and automated systems?
questions.why_live: rev0014 adds a delegation-discipline rule, but the archive still has not mapped which functions may be mediated safely and which must remain more directly owned by the claiming office or institution.

questions.question: What institutional designs let righteous equity correct rule-underfit without reopening patronage, arbitrariness, or covert favoritism?
questions.why_live: rev0016 adds an equity discipline, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive criteria for when equitable correction is required, when straight sameness is enough, and what safeguards keep particular correction from collapsing into special pleading.

questions.question: When is righteous interruption satisfied by internal objection, recusal, or protected disclosure, and when does it require resignation, withdrawal of cooperation, or burdened public disobedient witness?
questions.why_live: rev0017 admits interruption into canon, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive thresholds for when continued participation becomes complicit enough to require exit or public breach rather than narrower internal correction.

questions.question: When is mercy righteous rather than a disguised pardon for the powerful, and when is sanction still due even after apology, repair, or victim forgiveness?
questions.why_live: rev0018 adds a starter mercy/sanction rule, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive criteria for when censure, exclusion, penalty, restorative path, or clemency best fits the due without shifting hidden costs onto victims or the public.

questions.question: In which public domains does the archive's public-trust / fiduciary cue remain only analogical, and in which domains might stronger fiduciary treatment actually fit?
questions.why_live: rev0019 admits a qualified public-trust / nonownership rule for office, but the archive still has not mapped where fiduciary theorizing fits structurally and where it over-imports private-law assumptions into public life.

questions.question: When, if ever, can emergency action near or beyond ordinary jurisdictional limits still count as righteous, and what ratification, review, disclosure, sunset, or repair must follow for it not to collapse into office usurpation?
questions.why_live: rev0020 adds bearer, competence, and authority-bounds discipline, but the archive still lacks role-sensitive criteria for distinguishing righteous emergency burden-taking from mere unauthorized expansion of office power.

questions.question: When does righteousness require direct hearing or consent from those burdened, when is accountable representation enough, and what urgency- or incapacity-based substitutes are strong enough not to collapse into over-the-head rule?
questions.why_live: rev0021 adds an affected-standing rule, but the archive still lacks domain-sensitive criteria for direct participation, accountable representation, guardianship, sampling, and post hoc review across courts, agencies, legislatures, emergencies, and institutions acting over diffuse publics.

questions.question: Which proxy, guardianship, or stewardship structures are strong enough to carry the claims of children, supported decision-makers, diffuse publics, and future persons without overwriting them?
questions.why_live: rev0022 adds an absent-claimant / proxy-voice / stewardship rule, but the archive still lacks domain-sensitive criteria for when direct support, accountable representation, substituted judgment, best-interest protection, trusteeship, or future-facing stewardship is the right fit.

questions.question: When do special ties — family, friendship, constituency, covenant, promise, or membership — rightly thicken what is due, and when must public roles instead answer those ties with recusal, disclosure, or anti-nepotism restraint?
questions.why_live: rev0023 admits a bounded-partiality rule, but the archive still lacks a tradition- and role-sensitive map of when special obligations intensify righteousness, when they are permissions only, and when public office must suppress them.
